HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. KOREAN FACES on everyone in frame: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black); a low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European nose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. KOREAN WEBTOON character-introduction splash, dramatic manhwa COVER. Intimate medium, slight dutch, Alchun’s FACE large. DARK HEAVILY GRASSY FOREST like a survival test: waist-high wet grass, dense trunks, one shaft. NO nets. ONE device: his two hands locking on bark in the foreground — NORMAL teenage hands from the attached portrait, NOT stick-thin, NOT extra-long. Alchun FIFTEEN, lean, frightened, teal po over crimson with the SAME shoulder-and-sleeve volume as the portrait. A NEW expression: fear then the decision. Living eyes WHITE sclera BLACK pupil. Teal and one crimson flash. No tiger yet. No text. No watermark. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = alchun. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels). KOREAN FACES on every person, named or extra: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, honey, gold, blue, grey, green or purple). Never paint the entire eyeball solid black. A low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European, Roman or Persian nose. East Asian bone: single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair. Never Western, Latin, or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes. ALCHUN — Look: Broader, rounder face than Bidam or Yushin; warm half-smile, a red liner wing at the outer eye; as a boy no scar and no grey. Adult: grey tied back under a dark headband, a red scar cutting the left temple, thin goatee. Unmistakably Korean: BLACK eyes (never brown, blue or grey), a low soft Korean nasal bridge. Dress: Teal-green po. Hwarang: teal po over a crimson collar and crimson sash, teal crescent-moon headband, jougwan with two tan pheasant feathers. Councillor: teal po over a rust-red inner robe, dark sash, no jougwan. High Councillor: white dragon-embroidered overcoat over magenta, teal headband. Now: Boy hwarang, FIFTEEN: leaner than Yushin and Bidam, frightened until he isn't; rounder face, no grey, no scar, teal over crimson. BODY matches the attached /ch_alchun_hwarang.png: normal teenage Korean proportions, broad shoulders under the teal sleeves, arms the right length. NOT noodle-thin, NOT extra-long arms, NOT a stick figure. Colour #8fb3e0. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
